clue.text: Hands over exchanged item

indicators.note: over signals that the word for hands is turned the other way round

parts.note: paws are hands, informally

explanation.surface: Someone hands over an item in an exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' reads as part of 'hands over' but signals the reversal of PAWS.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a trade, or the thing traded in one, is a swap.

clue.text: Oddly found on meadow, one plant usually among trees?

indicators.note: oddly means arranged in a strange way, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Something found unusually on a meadow is normally a woodland plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' tempts you to take alternate letters, but here it means rearranged, acting on the meadow phrase; 'found' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This spring flower is a woodland plant, so it usually grows among trees, as the question mark hints.

clue.text: Stop drinking endless beer it's common

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to prevent is to stop

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the word for beer is dropped

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: Stopping someone drinking beer is a common thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drinking' signals a container, and 'endless' cuts the last letter from the beer; 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent is widespread, which is to say common.

clue.text: Maybe gossip about old students finally became slander

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a cat is a spiteful gossiping person, so maybe a gossip
alumni are former students of a school or college

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Gossip about former students turned into slander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe gossip' is a cat in the old sense of a spiteful woman; 'about' makes it surround the old students, and 'finally' takes the end of 'became'.
explanation.definitionFit: To calumniate is to make false and damaging statements, a formal synonym of the verb slander.

clue.text: Scottish historian who's given a hearing in English city

indicators.note: given a hearing signals that a word is spoken and its sound is what counts

parts.note: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, in the north-west of England

explanation.surface: A Scottish historian gets a public hearing in an English city.
explanation.walkthrough: Carlisle is a cathedral city near the Scottish border; the historian's name sounds the same.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Carlyle was a nineteenth-century Scottish historian and essayist, author of The French Revolution.

clue.text: All harangue kid —- I, being different, chortle raucously

indicators.note: being different means the letters are put into another order

explanation.surface: Someone harangues a child and, being contrary, cackles loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being different' rearranges ALL HARANGUE KID I, all fifteen letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to laugh loudly and harshly, like the gurgle of water down a plughole, which is a raucous chortle.

clue.text: Messy remedy offered by doctor going round upper-class spa

indicators.note: going round means one piece encloses another

parts.note: MD is a Doctor of Medicine
U is the old abbreviation for upper-class
Bath is the English spa city

explanation.surface: A doctor prescribes a messy treatment while touring a posh spa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' makes the doctor enclose the upper-class letter; Bath is a Somerset city famous for its Roman spa.
explanation.definitionFit: A bath in mineral-rich mud is a spa treatment, and a dirty one: a messy remedy.

clue.text: A Greek star outshining the others

definitions.meaning: the first letter of the Greek alphabet, an A in Greek
in star naming, the brightest star of a constellation takes the first Greek letter

explanation.surface: A Greek celebrity shines brighter than everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from the first Greek letter, which also labels a constellation's brightest star.

clue.text: Den's deficiency — no roof

indicators.note: in a down answer the roof is the top letter, so the first letter goes

parts.note: a dearth is a shortage or deficiency

explanation.surface: A den's drawback is that it has no roof.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the 'roof' is the first letter, so D leaves DEARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's burrow, its den, is called an earth.

clue.text: Soldiers restricted by mist enveloping nearby territory

indicators.note: restricted by means the soldiers are held inside the next word

parts.note: fog is a thick mist
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
round, as a preposition, means surrounding or enveloping

explanation.surface: Troops hemmed in by mist that surrounds the nearby area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricted by' puts the soldiers inside the mist; 'enveloping' gives the preposition meaning surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: The foreground is the part of a scene nearest the viewer, the closest ground.

clue.text: Incentive to knock time off sprint

indicators.note: to knock something off is to remove it, so a letter is taken away
off completes the phrase knock off, meaning the letter is removed

parts.note: a spurt is a short sprint

explanation.surface: A runner is encouraged to cut time off a sprint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knock ... off' removes T from SPURT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spur is a goad, so figuratively an incentive or stimulus.

clue.text: Bird by a railway — it's a sort of finch

parts.note: bird is slang for prison, and so is can

explanation.surface: A bird beside a railway line turns out to be a type of finch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' is prison slang here (doing bird), not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow cage bird is a member of the finch family, native to the Atlantic islands.

clue.text: The man touching a bull gets skin complaint

parts.note: he refers to a man
bull means nonsense, as does trash

explanation.surface: A man who touches a bull comes out in a skin condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bull' is the slang for nonsense, not the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Prickly heat, an itchy rash brought on by hot weather, is a skin complaint.

clue.text: Food ingredient that could make gateau a mess

indicators.note: could make means these letters can be formed into something else

explanation.surface: Something that might turn a gateau into a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could make' rearranges GATEAU A MESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced seasoned meat used to fill sausages or stuffing is a cooking ingredient.

clue.text: Something planted in ground is said to bring this yield

indicators.note: is said signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: a seed is something planted in soil

explanation.surface: Something planted in soil is said to give a crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yield' seems to belong to the crop picture, but it is the verb meaning give way.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or surrender, which is a sense of yield.

clue.text: Far end of the mine has gas in outer layer

indicators.note: far end of picks the last letter of the next word

parts.note: a pit is a mine
helium is a gas

explanation.surface: Deep in a mine there is gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Far end of the' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Epithelium is the tissue forming the surface layer of the body and organs, an outer layer.

clue.text: Craft displayed here may be brilliant

definitions.text: Craft displayed here may be brilliant

parts.words: Craft displayed here may be brilliant
parts.note: read as a vessel moored as a beacon: the craft that is shining here shows bright lamps to warn others

explanation.surface: A showcase where craftwork may be excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: A moored vessel carrying a beacon to guide ships is a brilliant craft, bright rather than clever.

clue.text: It's good, being in Europe? That's uncertain

indicators.note: being in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Continent is the British name for mainland Europe

explanation.surface: Is it good to be in Europe? That is doubtful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' puts G inside CONTINENT, which is what British speakers call mainland Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Contingent means dependent on chance or on something else, hence uncertain.

clue.text: Excellent black chap, set up to protect one African country

indicators.note: to protect means these pieces surround the letter for one
in a down answer, set up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
a man is a chap
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A fine black man stood up to defend an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to protect' puts I between AIB and MAN; 'set up' then turns AIBIMAN upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Namibia is a country in south-western Africa.

clue.text: One keeping any number in bird?

indicators.note: in means the number letter goes inside the bird

parts.note: a turkey is a bird
N stands for an indefinite number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone keeps a number of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One keeping' means a jailer, who keeps prisoners.
explanation.definitionFit: A turnkey is a jailer, one who keeps prisoners locked in.

clue.text: End journey by a lake

parts.note: to go is to journey

explanation.surface: A journey finishes beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A goal is an aim or objective, an end to be reached.

clue.text: We left — theatre production not entirely appreciated

indicators.note: not entirely means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a comedy is a theatre production

explanation.surface: We walked out of a show that was not entirely enjoyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not entirely' trims the Y from COMEDY.
explanation.definitionFit: If something was welcomed it was received gladly, that is, appreciated.

clue.text: Water may have drained from them? Plug is required

definitions.text: Water may have drained from them?

parts.note: a wad is a plug of material
taken as written

explanation.surface: Water may drain away, so a plug is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drained' suggests a sink, but the definition means dry river beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Wadis are desert watercourses that are dry except in the rainy season, so water has drained from them.

clue.text: Eliminate gangster upsetting S. American city

indicators.note: in a down answer, upsetting means the letters are turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: to zap is to destroy or eliminate
Al Capone was the archetypal gangster

explanation.surface: Wiping out a gangster upsets a South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsetting' turns ZAPAL to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: La Paz is the seat of government of Bolivia, in South America.

clue.text: Right beast!

parts.note: an otter is a beast

explanation.surface: An exclamation calling someone a real brute.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: 'right beast!' is a cry about a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A cad or scoundrel is a rotter, the sort one might call a right beast.

clue.text: Drug detected in underground operation

indicators.note: detected in means the answer is found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Drugs were found in an undercover operation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for a drug, especially cannabis.

clue.text: Has nothing to do with Uriah, ostracised family member

parts.note: to black something is to boycott it, to have nothing to do with it
Uriah Heep is the fawning clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield

explanation.surface: A family shuns Uriah, its outcast relation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black' is the trade-union verb meaning to boycott.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names the disgraced member of a family whom the rest disown.

clue.text: Zany ruse — it is concocted to get power

indicators.note: concocted means made up from ingredients, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild trick is devised to seize power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is concocted' rearranges ZANY RUSE IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Suzerainty is sovereign control over a dependent state, a kind of power.

clue.text: Head chef's preparation

definitions.meaning: an old word for the head, especially the crown
pâté is a spread of minced meat or fish made by a cook

explanation.surface: A head chef's dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the crown of the head, and a paste of minced liver or meat prepared by a chef.
